title: YouTube star Cliff Tan apologizes to angry fans after promoting AI for interior design
excerpt: Cliff Tan, who runs a popular interior design YouTube channel, posted a video promoting an AI company. His fans then revolted and he apologized.
content_html:
Another YouTube creator is facing online backlash over the use of artificial intelligence.

Cliff Tan, who runs a popular interior design YouTube channel called "Dear Modern" that has 2.4 million subscribers and a corresponding TikTok account with 3.6 million followers, posted a video on Monday in which he apologized for promoting an AI company.

"Yesterday I made a video on AI, and it disappointed many of you," Tan said in the video. "I'm really sorry about that."

Tan's apology comes a week after Hank Green, one of the internet's most reliable content creators, apologized to fans for relying on AI "too heavily" when researching his videos. He later shared a new AI policy for his channel.

In Tan's case, he posted a paid advertisement for a Chinese AI company called "Dreamina," which allows users to generate animated videos with written prompts. In the ad, Tan uploads hand-drawn sketches to the software before transforming them into an animated floor plan.

Though Tan uses his own sketches as source material and says in the video that he doesn't "like AI" because "it makes you forget to use your brain," the video was quickly flooded with negative comments.

"No, Mr. Cliff. Please. Don't sell yourself to AI," one comment with 1,700 likes reads. Others criticized the "Dreamina" company itself, which is owned by ByteDance.

In a follow-up comment on the ad, Tan said he thought the software "would be genuinely useful to fellow designers."

"I just don't want you guys, with the right sentiments, to be martyrs in a world that is increasingly leaving us behind," he wrote.

As tech companies push AI to become a ubiquitous part of daily life, critics worry it could impact critical thinking skills. In 2025, a survey published by Workday found that nearly half of respondents worried the tech would cause a decline in critical thinking.

AI also threatens to upend the workforce as companies of varying stripes race to integrate AI into their workflows.

Last year, the British Institute of Interior Design said AI "has a growing presence in interior design."

Stephen Dick, the founder of an interior design firm in the UK, told the institute that "the possibilities are impressive" with text-to-image visualization tools.

"I know of many designers using text-to-image visualization tools, too," Dick was quoted as saying.

Neither Dreamina, based in Beijing, nor Tan, who is based in Singapore, immediately responded to a request for comment from Business Insider made outside their normal business hours.

content_html_zh:
另一位 YouTube 创作者因使用人工智能而面临网络强烈反对。

Cliff Tan 运营着一个名为“Dear Modern”的 YouTube 流行室内设计频道，该频道拥有 240 万订阅者，相应的 TikTok 帐户拥有 360 万粉丝。他于周一发布了一段视频，在视频中他为宣传一家人工智能公司而道歉。

“昨天我制作了一个关于人工智能的视频，它让你们很多人感到失望，”谭在视频中说道。 “对此我真的很抱歉。”

谭的道歉是在互联网上最可靠的内容创作者之一汉克·格林（Hank Green）向粉丝道歉后一周做出的，因为他在研究他的视频时“过于依赖”人工智能。 后来他分享了他频道的新人工智能政策。

以谭为例，他为一家名为“Dreamina”的中国人工智能公司发布了付费广告，该广告允许用户生成带有书面提示的动画视频。 在广告中，谭将手绘草图上传到软件，然后将其转换为动画平面图。

尽管谭使用自己的草图作为源材料，并在视频中表示他不“喜欢人工智能”，因为“它会让你忘记使用你的大脑”，但视频很快就充斥着负面评论。

“不，克里夫先生。 请。 不要把自己卖给人工智能。”一条获得 1,700 点赞的评论写道。 其他人则批评字节跳动旗下的“Dreamina”公司本身。

在对该广告的后续评论中，谭说他认为该软件“对其他设计师来说确实有用”。

他写道：“我只是不希望你们怀着正确的情感，成为这个日益把我们抛在后面的世界的烈士。”

随着科技公司推动人工智能成为日常生活中无处不在的一部分，批评者担心它可能会影响批判性思维技能。 2025 年，Workday 发布的一项调查发现，近一半的受访者担心该技术会导致批判性思维能力下降。

随着不同类型的公司竞相将人工智能整合到他们的工作流程中，人工智能也有可能颠覆劳动力。

去年，英国室内设计协会表示，人工智能“在室内设计中的应用越来越广泛”。

英国一家室内设计公司的创始人斯蒂芬·迪克（Stephen Dick）告诉该研究所，文本到图像可视化工具的“可能性令人印象深刻”。

“我知道许多设计师也使用文本到图像的可视化工具，”迪克说道。

总部位于北京的 Dreamina 和总部位于新加坡的 Tan 都没有立即回应《商业内幕》在正常工作时间之外提出的置评请求。
